blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in South Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering about the cost of a home extension in South Melbourne? We break down pricing, council fees, and timeline factors for 2026.
body: Planning a home extension in South Melbourne in 2026? You're not alone. With property values rising and families needing more space, extending your existing home is often more cost-effective than moving. But what does it actually cost? Let's break it down based on current market rates and local factors.

A typical single-storey extension in South Melbourne ranges from $3,000 to $5,000 per square metre, depending on complexity. A two-storey add-on can push closer to $6,000 per square metre. This includes foundations, framing, roofing, and basic finishes. High-end finishes like stone benchtops and custom joinery will increase the total.

Council fees in South Melbourne (City of Port Phillip) are another major factor. You'll need a building permit and possibly a planning permit if you're altering the footprint. Expect to budget $3,000 to $10,000 for permits and compliance reports. A good builder will handle all of this for you.

Labour costs in Melbourne have risen due to high demand and material supply issues. Skilled trades like carpenters and bricklayers charge between $60 and $90 per hour. However, most builders quote on a fixed-price basis, so you won't face hourly surprises. Always get at least three quotes.

Site conditions matter. If your South Melbourne property has clay soils, you may need deeper footings, adding $10,000 to $20,000 to the project. Similarly, demolishing an existing structure or dealing with heritage overlays will increase costs. Heritage overlays are common in parts of South Melbourne.

Timing is crucial. A typical extension takes 4 to 6 months from start to finish, but delays can happen due to weather, material shortages, or council approvals. Plan for a 6-month timeline to be safe. Start your conversations early—ideally 3 months before you want to break ground.

Financing your extension is easier than you think. Many homeowners use equity release from their home loan. Others opt for construction loans that pay out in stages. Talk to your bank or a mortgage broker about your options before committing.

In summary, a well-planned home extension in South Melbourne can add significant value to your property. With a fixed-price contract and an experienced builder like Hutchinson Builders, you'll avoid nasty surprises. Contact us for a free quote tailored to your project.

blogPosts.title: Top 5 Commercial Building Trends in Melbourne for 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Stay ahead with the latest commercial building trends in Melbourne. From Green Star to flexible workspaces, here's what's shaping the industry.
body: Commercial construction in Melbourne is evolving fast. As businesses return to the office and sustainability becomes a priority, building owners are adapting. Here are the top five trends shaping commercial projects in 2026.

Green Star certification is now a baseline for many projects. Tenants demand energy-efficient buildings with lower running costs. Features like solar panels, rainwater harvesting, and high-performance glazing are standard. Hutchinson Builders delivered a 5 Star Green Star project at 420 on Flinders.

Flexible workspaces are here to stay. Open-plan layouts with modular furniture allow businesses to reconfigure their space as needs change. We're seeing more breakout areas, collaboration zones, and quiet rooms. This trend is especially strong in South Melbourne and Docklands.

Mixed-use developments are booming. Combining offices, retail, and residential in one site creates vibrant communities. Think Howard Smith Wharves—a perfect example of mixed-use done right. These projects require careful planning and a builder who understands all three sectors.

Health and wellness features are no longer optional. Improved air filtration, natural light, and biophilic design (plants and green walls) are expected. Studies show these features boost productivity and reduce sick days. Owners who invest in wellness attract premium tenants.

Technology integration is key. Smart building systems manage lighting, HVAC, and security from a central platform. Tenants can book meeting rooms and adjust their environment via an app. We're installing these systems in new builds and retrofitting them in older structures.

Material costs remain volatile, but savvy builders are locking in prices early. Using prefabricated components can reduce on-site labour and speed up timelines. Hutchinson Builders use modular methods on select projects to keep costs predictable.

If you're planning a commercial build in Melbourne, partner with a builder who understands these trends. We'll help you design a space that's efficient, attractive, and future-proof. Get in touch for a no-obligation chat.

blogPosts.title: What to Know Before Building a Warehouse in Port Melbourne
blogPosts.excerpt: Building an industrial warehouse in Port Melbourne? Learn about zoning, slab design, height limits, and cost factors from experienced local builders.
body: Port Melbourne is a prime location for industrial and logistics facilities, being close to the port and freeway access. If you're planning to build a warehouse there, there are several factors to consider before breaking ground. Here's what you need to know.

Zoning is the first hurdle. Most of Port Melbourne is zoned for industrial use, but overlays and restrictions vary. Council will require a planning permit for anything over a certain size. Check the City of Port Phillip's planning scheme early to avoid delays.

Slab design is critical for warehouses. Heavy-duty concrete slabs must support racking systems and forklifts. We typically specify a 150mm to 200mm thick slab with steel reinforcement. The subgrade must be tested for bearing capacity, especially if the site has fill or clay.

Height limits are often overlooked. Some areas have restrictions on building height, especially near residential zones. Port Melbourne industrial zones generally allow heights up to 15 metres, but it's best to confirm with council. High-clearance warehouses need specific design approvals.

Drainage and stormwater management are key. Industrial sites generate runoff that must be treated on-site. You may need detention tanks or rain gardens. Factor in $20,000 to $50,000 for stormwater compliance, depending on site size.

Fire safety requirements are stringent for warehouses. Sprinkler systems, fire hydrants, and emergency access are mandatory. The building code requires certain fire ratings for walls and roofing. Your builder will coordinate with fire engineers.

Material and equipment access is another consideration. Ensure your site has adequate truck turning space and loading docks. A site with limited access may require special approvals and increase construction costs.

Hutchinson Builders has delivered multiple industrial projects, including the $125M NewCold Melbourne II cold storage facility. We know the local councils, suppliers, and conditions. Contact us for a free consultation on your Port Melbourne warehouse project.

blogPosts.title: How to Choose the Right Builder for Your Apartment Development in South Melbourne
blogPosts.excerpt: Selecting a builder for your apartment development in South Melbourne is critical. We explain what to look for in terms of experience, contracts, and local know-how.
body: Choosing a builder for a multi-unit residential project in South Melbourne is one of the most important decisions you'll make. The right partner will deliver on time, on budget, and to high standards. Here's a guide to help you choose wisely.

Look for experience with similar projects. A builder who has completed mid-rise or high-rise apartments understands the complexities of structural engineering, fire safety, and amenity spaces. Check their portfolio for projects like Chester & Ella or The Landmark.

Fixed-price contracts provide certainty. Avoid builders who offer only cost-plus agreements, as they leave you exposed to overruns. A reputable builder will quote a fixed price for the entire project, with clear inclusions and exclusions.

Local knowledge is invaluable. Builders who work regularly in South Melbourne know the council's requirements for setbacks, height limits, and heritage overlays. They can streamline approvals and avoid costly redesigns at the last minute.

Check their safety record. Ask about their incident rate and safety training programs. A builder with a strong safety culture is likely to be more organised and reliable overall. Hutchinson Builders have a dedicated safety team on every site.

Communication matters. You want a builder who provides regular updates and is easy to reach. Ask for references from past clients and speak to them about their experience. Did the builder communicate well? Were there any surprises?

Subcontractor relationships are important too. A builder who works with trusted, long-term subcontractors ensures consistent quality on site. Ask who will be doing the structural work, plumbing, and electrical.

Finally, trust your gut. If a builder seems too salesy or lacks transparency, move on. A good builder will be happy to answer your questions and provide documentation. We're proud of our 105-year track record.
